public_rationale: Participant accounts and sworn testimony connect specific Altman communications to directors' concerns. They support the modest conclusion that his conduct contributed to lost trust. This does not establish that every allegation was true or that dismissal was warranted. Marcus's inference from OpenAI's silence would be insufficient by itself; the affirmative records provide the support.
limitations: The directors were participants in the dispute.
The available investigation account did not establish that Altman's conduct required removal.
Causal contribution is supported without assigning exclusive blame.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Sam Altman's actions played at least some role in the breakdown of trust with OpenAI's board.

statement.excerpt: Given that OpenAI put this line about “breakdown in trust” (but not the full report) on their own website, and given that OpenAI did not find enough to say that the breakdown in trust was purely in the Board’s imagination, we can safely conclude that actions by Sam Altman did play at least some role in that breakdown of trust.
statement.document_title: Disturbing and misleading efforts to defame Helen Toner through misdirection

from_speaker: did play at least some role
our_interpretation: Some role means a contributing cause, not the sole cause or conduct sufficient to justify dismissal.
The claim concerns the relationship breakdown culminating in the November 17, 2023 firing.
A company's failure to deny misconduct is not affirmative evidence. Participant accounts and documented conduct must carry the causal assessment.
criteria.support_condition: Investigation findings or corroborating participant records connect identifiable Altman conduct to the board's loss of trust.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that Altman's conduct contributed nothing and that the breakdown arose entirely independently of his actions.
